old: Algae are simple, thalloid, autotrophic and mostly aquatic. Chlorophyceae are green algae with chlorophyll a and b, starch and a cellulose wall. Phaeophyceae are brown algae with chlorophyll a and c and fucoxanthin; they store laminarin or mannitol and have algin walls. Rhodophyceae are red algae with chlorophyll a and d and r-phycoerythrin; they store floridean starch and have no flagella. Bryophytes are the amphibians of the plant kingdom. Their dominant gametophyte bears antheridia and archegonia, the sporophyte depends on it, and a protonema stage occurs in mosses. Pteridophytes are the first vascular land plants. The sporophyte is dominant and the prothallus is the gametophyte. Gymnosperms have naked ovules. They are heterosporous, and their male and female gametophytes stay within sporangia retained on the sporophyte.

Their dominant gametophyte bears antheridia and archegonia, the sporophyte depends on it, and a protonema stage occurs in mosses. Pteridophytes are the first vascular land plants. The sporophyte is dominant and the prothallus is the gametophyte. Gymnosperms have naked ovules. They are heterosporous, and their male and female gametophytes stay within sporangia retained on the sporophyte.
fixes: Brown algae have a cellulosic wall with an outer algin coating, not algin walls

old: Animals are classified by several bases. The first is level of organisation: cellular in Porifera, tissue in Cnidaria, organ in Platyhelminthes and organ system in the others. The second is symmetry: asymmetrical, radial or bilateral. The third is germ layers: diploblastic in Porifera, Cnidaria and Ctenophora, triploblastic in the rest. The fourth is coelom: acoelomate in Platyhelminthes, pseudocoelomate in Aschelminthes and true coelom from Annelida onwards. The fifth is metamerism, first seen in Annelida. Radial symmetry means any plane through the central axis divides the body into identical halves. The non-chordate phyla are Porifera, Cnidaria, Ctenophora, Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata and Hemichordata. Each has hallmark features such as choanocytes, cnidoblasts, comb plates, flame cells, nephridia, Malpighian tubules, radula and the water vascular system.
